articles.title: Democrats Call for Probe Into Military Leaders as U.S. Army Whistleblower Alleges Warnings Were Dismissed Ahead of Deadly Iran Attack
articles.summary: An American soldier has alleged that U.S. military leaders dismissed concerns ahead of an Iranian attack that killed six servicemembers on March 1. The complaint, submitted Friday to the House and Senate Armed Services committees and first reported by CBS on Sunday, alleges that U.S. Army leaders did not heed warnings about thin fortifications at a command post at Kuwait’s Port Shuaiba. articles.title: In Hakeem Jeffries’ Rise to Speaker, Black Leaders See a Milestone—and a Test
articles.summary: In 1870, Joseph Rainey of South Carolina became the first Black person to serve in the U.S. House. This week, current and newly elected House Democrats are poised to meet to select Rep. Hakeem Jeffries as the chamber’s first Black Speaker. It is a moment fraught with meaning and hurdles for both the New York Democrat and the larger Black community, multiple Black leaders tell TIME. articles.title: Trump’s Golf Course Plans Hit a Legal Obstacle: His Own Social Media Posts
articles.summary: President Donald Trump faced a legal setback on Saturday when a federal judge temporarily blocked the planned closure of a public golf course and surrounding parkland in Washington, D.C. Among the evidence undermining his Administration’s justification: his own Truth Social posts. articles.title: All Hail Philomena Cunk, the Perfect Fake Newswoman for Our Age of Ignorance
articles.summary: In the future, when some documentary series in whatever medium succeeds television looks back at the current decade in public discourse, it might name our era the Age of Ignorance. articles.title: Air Traffic Control Systems Are Outdated. What’s Being Done to Prevent Another Outage?
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Saturday blamed the previous day’s nationwide ground stop on the replacement of copper wires at a “remote” Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) facility. Installing new fiber optic lines led to critical communication breakdowns, he said. About 7,500 flights were delayed and over 9,000 were canceled on Friday, according to FlightAware .
